findings.summary: The account of B40's 13 denials leaves one denial unclassified.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261126-1008-b42-i162-fence-reads-pwsh.loop-brief.md:28-31 names 11 subshell denials and one $env denial; the B40 session records contain those plus one `command substitution cannot be judged` denial at .vloop/state/runs/B20261125-2207-b40-i156-mixed-os-pwsh/20261126-000247/sessions/005-review.json:23. Counting the three reason texts across the run gives 11 subshell, 1 command-substitution and 1 $env denial.
findings.fix: State the complete breakdown: 11 subshell/process-substitution denials, one command-substitution denial, and one $env denial. Clarify that W3 reads the first and third syntax families' targeted common forms while command substitution remains refused with W4 guidance.

decisions: Keep parity with sh rather than building a broader pwsh sandbox; I agree, given S-2 and the stated advisory role of the fence.
Judge pwsh, powershell and cmd command-string wrappers instead of refusing the wrappers outright; I agree.
Refuse pwsh script blocks rather than parse them; I agree because the brief supplies explicit alternatives.
Read only parenthesized property access and literal $env assignment among the pwsh forms; I agree, with the B40 breakdown corrected above.
Treat cmd command strings with the existing splitter and refuse %, ^ and unresolved wrappers; I agree.
Apply W2-W4 to the powershell tool and to a W1 pwsh/powershell string under either tool; I agree and find the scope stated.
Update the guide and fence audit, but no skills; I agree.
Pin the proposed long-help wording and regenerate docs/guide/commands.md; I agree.
Leave pwsh file cmdlet paths and & ./script.ps1 unjudged under the parity decision; I agree.
